newsitem.title: THAILAND: U.S. pilot reaches Bangkok on Earhart tribute trip.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pilot reaches Bangkok on Earhart tribute trip.

text.p: American woman pilot Linda Finch arrived in Bangkok on Friday to a grand welcome after crossing the half-way mark in her bid to emulate the legendary Amelia Earhart's around-the-world journey 60 years ago.
Finch arrived from northern Chiang Mai in a 1935 Lockheed Electra 10E, the same model used by Earhart who vanished between New Guinea and Howland Island in the Pacific in 1937.

"I think Amelia was a great heroine in our time. This aircraft is the same model that was built 62 years ago, the only difference is that this plane has been equipped with modern electronic gear," Finch told about 200 people who had gathered at the airport to greet her.
The plane, one of only two remaining, was painstakingly restored for "World Flight 1997", a $4.5 million project.
Finch's journey will last two and a half months, cover a total distance of 26,748 miles (43,045 km), and span five continents.

The Texas businesswoman and aviator began her odyssey on March 17 from the same hangar in Oakland, California, from which Earhart and her navigator Fred Noonan departed on their round the world flight attempt.

Finch, due to continue her flight to Singapore, Indonesia and Australia through Honolulu and return to Oakland in late May, said her route mirrored Earhart's. The only difference was that she did not go via Burma and stop there like Earhart did.
"I did not go to Burma because of the political situation there and I was told not to go," Finch said.
The United States has slapped sanctions on new American investments in Burma which is ruled by a military government accused of suppressing democracy and human rights.
